M6_S01.summary: Kamma is intentional action, and in Abhidhamma terms it is nothing other than the mental factor of volition working through body, speech and mind.
body: Kamma means action, the intention that produces action. In terms of ultimate realities, kamma is precisely the mental factor of volition (Cetanā): the deliberate intention behind a deed.
The Buddha declared: 'Cetanāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ vadāmi' — 'Monks, it is volition that I call kamma.'
Kamma arises through three doors: body, speech and mind. Of the three, mental kamma is reckoned the weightiest, since both bodily and verbal action are set in motion by the mind.

Six roots are the origin of kamma: greed, hatred and delusion on the unwholesome side, and non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion on the wholesome. As the text has it, 'Lobho nidānaṃ kammānaṃ samudayāya' — greed is the origin from which kammas arise.

M6_S02.summary: The Kammacatukka arranges sixteen kinds of kamma in four groups of four: by function, by priority of ripening, by time of ripening and by sphere of ripening.
body: The Kammacatukka divides kamma into four groups of four, sixteen kinds in all.
Group one — by function (kiccavasena): reproductive kamma, supportive kamma, obstructive kamma and destructive kamma.
Group two — by strength, that is, the order in which kammas take their turn to ripen (pākadānapariyāyena): weighty kamma, death-proximate kamma, habitual kamma and cumulative kamma.
Group three — by time of ripening (pākakālavasena): immediately effective kamma, subsequently effective kamma, indefinitely effective kamma and defunct kamma.
Group four — by the sphere in which the result appears (pākaṭṭhānavasena): unwholesome kamma, sense-sphere wholesome kamma, form-sphere wholesome kamma and formless-sphere wholesome kamma.

M6_S03.summary: By function, kamma produces a life, sustains it, hinders it or cuts it off: reproductive, supportive, obstructive and destructive kamma.
body: Reproductive kamma (Janakakamma) is the kamma that generates the mental and material aggregates at rebirth-linking, bringing the resultant citta into being — that is, the rebirth-linking consciousness (Paṭisandhi viññāṇa).

Supportive kamma (Upatthambhakakamma) assists, nourishes and props up the reproductive kamma, keeping the aggregates in continuous succession. It is of the same kind as the reproductive kamma, wholesome or unwholesome, and continues until the death consciousness arises.

Obstructive kamma (Upapīḷakakamma) hinders the reproductive kamma, weakening its force and delaying its result. It is always of the opposite kind to the reproductive kamma. The source notes expressly that obstructive kamma does not occur in the form and formless realms.

Destructive kamma (Upaghātakakamma) cuts off other kammas, or cuts off their results. It is stronger than obstructive kamma: obstructive kamma merely hinders, whereas destructive kamma annihilates the reproductive kamma altogether.

M6_S04.summary: In the order of ripening, weighty kamma comes first, then death-proximate, then habitual, and only last the light cumulative kamma.
body: Weighty kamma (Garukakamma) is grave kamma whose result is certain and which no other kamma can forestall. On the unwholesome side it comprises the five heinous crimes (killing one's mother, killing one's father, killing an Arahant, causing a schism in the Sangha, and drawing the blood of a Buddha) together with fixed wrong view. On the wholesome side it is the nine sublime wholesome cittas, the form-sphere and formless-sphere jhānas.

According to the source, the unwholesome weighty kammas rank in strength as follows: fixed wrong view is the gravest, then causing a schism in the Sangha, then drawing the blood of a Buddha, and then patricide and matricide, their order depending on the moral standing of the parent.

Death-proximate kamma (Āsannakamma) is a wholesome or unwholesome kamma arising close to death — the last active cognitive process of the life, which conditions the life to come. Contrary cases occur: one who habitually did good may recall an evil deed at the last moment and be reborn in a woeful state, or the reverse; but no kamma already performed is lost on that account.

Habitual kamma (Āciṇṇakamma) is wholesome or unwholesome action performed so regularly that it becomes a habit and shapes the whole tenor of a person's life. If there is no weighty kamma, what one has habitually done is what comes back to mind at the close of life and so becomes the death-proximate kamma.

Cumulative kamma (Kaṭattākamma) covers all the actions that fall outside the previous three: slight kamma which usually produces no result, and which ripens only when there is no weighty or habitual kamma to take priority.

M6_S05.summary: Time of ripening is determined by the seven impulsion moments: the first gives a result in this life, the seventh in the next, the middle five at any time thereafter.
body: Kamma classified by time (Pākakālakamma) is determined with reference to the impulsion phase of the cognitive process — the seven javana moments.

The first impulsion is the weakest, since it arises first with no preceding impulsion of its own kind to support it. It can therefore give its result only in this very life: immediately effective kamma (Diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakamma). If it does not ripen within this life it becomes defunct.

The seventh impulsion is next weakest, standing at the point of dissolution. It yields its result in the life immediately following: subsequently effective kamma (Upapajjavedanīyakamma). If the second life passes without its ripening, it too becomes defunct.

The five middle impulsions, the second to the sixth, give results at no fixed time, from the third life onward until final Nibbāna: indefinitely effective kamma (Aparāpariyavedanīyakamma). Among them the fourth impulsion is the strongest, standing at the peak of the series.

Defunct kamma (Ahosikamma) is kamma that has been performed but never yields a result. The source stresses that indefinitely effective kamma does not ordinarily perish before it has given its result: 'Aparāparavedanīyaṃ pana vipākaṃ adatvā na nassati.'

M6_S06.summary: By sphere of ripening, kamma is unwholesome, sense-sphere wholesome, form-sphere wholesome or formless-sphere wholesome — the last two being purely mental kamma made in meditation.
body: Unwholesome kamma belongs to the sense sphere; in terms of ultimate realities it is the volition in the twelve unwholesome cittas. Except for the citta associated with restlessness, unwholesome kamma leads to rebirth in the woeful planes; all twelve, however, can give results in the course of a life.
Sense-sphere wholesome kamma is the volition in the eight sense-sphere beautiful wholesome cittas, and it leads to rebirth in the happy planes of the sense sphere.
Form-sphere wholesome kamma is purely mental kamma, made by the work of meditation, and it is divided into five grades according to the jhāna factors.
Formless-sphere wholesome kamma is likewise mental kamma made in meditation, divided into four grades according to the meditation subject taken as object.

The source also lists the ten bases of meritorious action in the sense sphere: giving, virtue, meditation, reverence towards elders, service, sharing one's merit, rejoicing in the merit of others, listening to the Dhamma, teaching the Dhamma, and straightening one's view.

M6_S07.summary: Through the three doors there are ten unwholesome courses of action and ten wholesome ones, each wholesome course being the abstinence from its unwholesome counterpart.
body: Three unwholesome courses belong to the body door: killing (Pāṇātipāta), stealing (Adinnādāna) and sexual misconduct (Kāmesumicchācāra).
Four belong to the speech door: false speech (Musāvāda), divisive speech (Pisuṇavācā), harsh speech (Pharusavācā) and idle chatter (Samphappalāpa).
Three belong to the mind door: covetousness (Abhijjhā), ill will (Byāpāda) and wrong view (Micchādiṭṭhi). These are mental deeds carried out by the mind alone, needing neither body nor speech.

As to their roots: killing, harsh speech and ill will spring from the root of hatred; sexual misconduct, covetousness and wrong view spring from the root of greed; the remaining four may spring from either root.

On the wholesome side, bodily good conduct is abstaining from the three above (through the factors of right action and right livelihood); verbal good conduct is abstaining from the four kinds of wrong speech (through right speech and right livelihood); and mental good conduct consists of non-covetousness (Anabhijjhā), non-ill-will (Abyāpāda) and right view (Sammādiṭṭhi).

M6_S08.summary: In terms of ultimate realities, 28 cittas generate reproductive kamma and 19 resultant cittas perform rebirth-linking, while kamma also produces eighteen kinds of materiality.
body: Twenty-eight cittas can generate reproductive kamma: 11 unwholesome cittas (the twelve less the delusion-rooted citta associated with restlessness, which gives no rebirth result), the 8 sense-sphere beautiful wholesome cittas, the 5 form-sphere wholesome cittas and the 4 formless-sphere wholesome cittas.

Nineteen cittas can perform rebirth-linking: the 2 rootless investigating cittas accompanied by equanimity (one unwholesome-resultant, one wholesome-resultant), the 8 sense-sphere beautiful resultant cittas, the 5 form-sphere resultant cittas and the 4 formless-sphere resultant cittas.

The volition in the 11 unwholesome cittas produces the rootless unwholesome-resultant investigating citta accompanied by equanimity — rebirth in the states of misery: as an animal, a ghost, an asura or a hell being.

Volition in the four sense-sphere wholesome cittas dissociated from knowledge, when the volition is weak, produces the rootless wholesome-resultant investigating citta — rebirth as a rootless human being in a happy plane; when it is strong, rebirth as a two-rooted person. Strong volition in the four wholesome cittas associated with knowledge produces rebirth as a three-rooted person.

Kamma also produces materiality: eighteen material phenomena are kamma-born — the 8 inseparable material phenomena, the 5 sensitive materialities, the space element, the material life faculty, the heart-base and the 2 sex materialities.
